title: Neural-DISCO: Source-Conditioned Counterfactual Editing of Neural Population Activity
abstract: arXiv:2610.33145v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Understanding how neural activity encodes behavioral and sensory variables is a key challenge in systems neuroscience. This requires models that go beyond predicting activity from labels and instead support source-conditioned counterfactual editing: given a recorded source response, we should be able to edit one measured behavioral or stimulus label and predict how neural activity would change while preserving other observed labels and source-specific variability not explained by the labels. Here, we introduce \textbf{Neural-DISCO}, a disentangled representation learning framework for counterfactual modeling of neural activity. Neural-DISCO partitions the latent space into label-specific components, each associated with an observed behavioral or stimulus label, together with a residual latent that captures variability not supplied through observed labels. translated_title: Neural-DISCO：源条件下的神经群体活动反事实编辑
translated_abstract: 理解神经活动如何编码行为与感觉变量是系统神经科学中的一个关键挑战。这需要超越“从标签预测活动”的模型，转而支持源条件下的反事实编辑：给定一段记录到的源响应，我们应当能够编辑某一个已测量的行为或刺激标签，并预测神经活动将如何变化，同时保持其他观测到的标签不变，并保留标签无法解释的源特异性变异性。在此，我们提出 Neural-DISCO——一个用于神经活动反事实建模的解耦表示学习框架。Neural-DISCO 将潜在空间划分为若干标签特异性成分（每个成分与一个观测到的行为或刺激标签相关联），以及一个捕获未被观测标签所提供变化性的残差潜变量。在模拟与真实神经记录数据集上，我们表明这一结构能够使……
tldr: Neural-DISCO 提出一种解耦表示学习框架，将神经活动的潜在空间分解为与各行为/刺激标签对应的成分和一个残差潜变量，从而实现源条件下的反事实编辑——在保持其他标签及源特异性变异不变的情况下，预测编辑某一标签后神经活动的变化。
